newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT, CRICKET-County play hardens Astle for coming tour.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT, CRICKET-County play hardens Astle for coming tour.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Aug 1 - Nathan Astle might be in the midst of the English county cricket competition but his mind is squarely set on New Zealand's coming busy summer in Zimbabwe, Australia and at home, Wellington's Evening Post newspaper reports.
"It's only really a month away and it is on my mind. It is going to be a testing summer and we will find out just where we are in the world," he said from England on Friday.
"We made a few steps forward last summer and with Flem (Stephen Fleming) as captain, and a good squad, I am sure we will continue to get better.
"The selectors have shown faith in players and that is good."

Astle has been improving during an unexpected stint with Nottinghamshire. He was called into the team when Pakistani newcomer Saqlain Mushtaq was injured. Astle found himself involved in the hectic hurly-burly of county cricket instead of his usual diet of league cricket.
Exposure to the day-in day-out routine of county cricket has been the making of many New Zealand players in the last 20 years and Astle is looking to continue that trend.

His bowling has benefited most. While something of a part-timer for New Zealand, he has a reasonable record with Canterbury and has found English conditions, particularly with the poor weather, suit his style.
Former England off-spinner Eddie Hemmings is the Nottinghamshire bowling coach and he has helped Astle work on his bowling.
"It has mainly been in trying out different grips and a little more variation in the pace of my bowling," Astle said.
"I've had a few scores here and there with my batting and it has been good experience on some testing tracks."
Astle posted his first county century in significant fashion against South African fast bowler Allan Donald's Warwickshire at a little over a run a ball.
"I have faced him before but it was good to come up against him again," Astle said.
"I also got a good look at the Australians in our game, which was good, given our tour there later in the year.
"They are a good solid attack and their bowlers are consistently good, and always at you.
"But in fact all the county bowlers are useful."
Surprising the county programme seemed a little more relaxed than New Zealand's season, Astle added.
"We have our 10 Shell Cup games and six four-day games and the pressure is on to perform. With the day-in day-out play over here, that pressure is not as great," he said.
"The standard is higher than the Shell series and it is definitely hard work disciplining yourself to get up every day and get back into it."
That has been a test of mental toughness, which he appreciates.
"But I am enjoying it. The Nottinghamshire players are a good bunch of guys and I can see why Cairnsy (Chris Cairns) enjoys it so much," he said.
Astle will have no problems getting released from the county to join the New Zealand team in Kenya for a season.
